no_new_module: No header or source is published. The one rule this packet recovers - that the scene-file entity reader canonicalises an authored localframe to s*R + t - belongs to 0046CF40 and 0085DC80, which are the scene-file/model territory a peer orchestrator owns. This packet reads them as a contract, as the brief directs, and does not reconstruct them; the follow-up packet scene_entity_reader_frames should own that arithmetic. Nothing else here is a new rule: 00B63D50's invertibility criterion is already implemented by derive_pose_affine_inverse_00b63d50 (include/bsp/pose_derived.hpp, packet orch3_pose_derived_i) and re-published by docs/MATRIX_ORTHOGONAL_INVERSE.md, and a predicate wrapping it would duplicate that. The result of this packet is evidence: a caller census and a shipped-data audit.
answer: A non-orthonormal local frame DOES reach entity+74h in the shipped game, so docs/MATRIX_ORTHOGONAL_INVERSE.md's bounded negative is superseded. 009258F0 has exactly two direct callers (009288D6, 00929C94, byte-level rel32 scan of all of .text) and is a virtual method in 30 vtables at slot +98h; both other implementations of that slot (00928860 in 44 vtables plus 3 ICF thunks, 00929C80 in 1) forward the localFrame argument verbatim, and 71 load-then-call dispatch sites exist (the single-instruction CALL [reg+98h] form occurs nowhere), 42 of which carry this hierarchy's world argument. The authored producer is the .scn localframe statement: BSP_SceneFile_ReadEntityBlock parses 16 floats at 0046D150, takes s = |row 0| at 0046D168..0046D1B0, orthonormalises through 0085DC80 at 0046D1BA, then multiplies the nine basis elements by s again at 0046D1BF..0046D222, and passes the buffer as the creator's localFrame at 0046D592/0046D5A4. The canonicalisation removes shear and per-row scale but PRESERVES a uniform scale, so the pose local is a similarity s*R + t, not an orthonormal frame. Across all 259 shipped .scn files, 7,621 of 133,655 localframe statements carry s outside 1 +/- 1e-3 (range 0.1586..3.0), including 105 anti-aircraft LandFort emplacements (s = 0.7069 on 'Heavy AA, Japanese 01') and 7 DestroyerGen placements ('L Hancock', s = 0.866). Because 0042D0D0 runs with normalize = 0, the gun reads asin(sin(theta)/s): a true 30 degree pitch reads 45.017 degrees at s = 0.7069 and 35.266 degrees at s = 0.866. Two shipped NavPoint frames author a zero row 2; 0085DC80's zero guard propagates that into two zero basis rows, the divide-by-zero case, but no gun sits under them. HierarchyMatrix, the other unvalidated path, copies 16 arbitrary floats from a property array pointer with no type or count check, but no shipped data file uses that key.

verification.direct_call_census: Exhaustive. local/scan_attach_refs.py parses the PE section table of I:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Battlestations Pacific/battlestationspacific.exe and tests EVERY byte offset of .text (00401000..00CE1136, raw 0x1000 + 0x8E1000) for an E8 or E9 whose site+5+rel32 equals 009258F0. Two E8 hits, zero E9 hits. Ghidra's xrefs confirms both but places 00929C94 at row 33, past the 25-row cap a sibling packet hit; the byte scan is the primary evidence.
verification.vtable_census: Exhaustive. The same scan, over every section with no alignment filter, finds the little-endian word F0 58 92 00 at 30 .rdata addresses. Slot offset +98h fixed two ways: fifteen sites sit 0x98 above a run of .text pointers terminated by a 00000000 word, and two ambiguous ones are fixed by the constructor that stores the vtable base (0065083A/00650852 store 00CF6250/00CF6218 in one constructor, 00CF62E8 - 00CF6250 = 0x98; 005193FB/0051949A store 00CEC578/00CEC5F0, 00CEC688 - 00CEC5F0 = 0x98). The naive backward walk over consecutive .text pointers over-reports the index when a sibling vtable abuts, which is why it was not trusted alone.
verification.dispatch_encoding_census: 0x98 > 0x7F so the displacement admits only disp32 (mod = 10). All four encodings tested over every byte of .text: FF /2 and FF /3 disp32 (CALL dword ptr [reg+98h]) = 0 sites; 8B /r disp32 followed within 32 bytes by CALL of that same register = 71 sites (443 instructions carry the disp32 at all); 8D /r disp32 (LEA reg,[reg+98h]) followed within 24 bytes by CALL dword ptr [reg] = 0; 81 /0 imm32 (ADD reg,98h) followed by CALL dword ptr [reg] = 0. Enumerating the encodings was necessary: the one-instruction form is used nowhere in this binary, so a scan for CALL [reg+98h] alone would have reported zero callers.
verification.argument_roles: From the RET 0Ch count and the body's own stores, not from the decompiler: 00925902 MOV EAX,[ESP+10h] then MOV [ESI+30h],EAX makes arg2 the world node; 0092592F MOV EAX,[ESP+0Ch] then MOV [ESI+3Ch],EAX makes arg1 the hierarchy parent; 009259BB MOV EAX,[ESP+14h] then PUSH EAX with LEA ECX,[ESI+74h] makes arg3 the local frame. The prologue is PUSH EBX; PUSH ESI only, so those three displacements are the three incoming stack arguments.
verification.esp_arithmetic: The two offsets that carry the finding are cross-checked against Ghidra's own stack naming. 0046CF40's prologue is PUSH -1 / PUSH 00C61E08 / PUSH FS:[0] (0x0C) + SUB ESP,190h + four register pushes (0x10), so the frame base is ESP_entry - 1ACh. Ghidra's local_164 is therefore base + 48h, exactly where 0046D15C FSTP [ESP+ESI*4+48h] writes, and local_10c is base + A0h. At 0046D592 two pushes have occurred, so LEA ECX,[ESP+50h] is base + 48h = local_164; at 0046D59D four pushes have occurred, so LEA EDX,[ESP+0B0h] is base + A0h = local_10c, which Ghidra shows as the name argument of BSP_SceneEntity_ShouldGenerate in the same block.
verification.x87_reading: 0046D168..0046D184 was read as assembly (the FLD/FMULP/FADDP schedule producing |row 0|^2) and then confirmed against Ghidra's decompilation of 0046CF40, which renders the same expression over local_164[0..2] and stores it before the 1e-10 compare. Two representations, not one.
verification.register_provenance: 0085DC80's row roles come from the whole listing, not one idiom: 0085DC85 MOV ESI,ECX, 0085DC87 LEA EBX,[ESI+20h] (float 8 = row 2, the normalisation reference) and 0085DCB9 LEA EDI,[ESI+10h] (float 4 = row 1). The zero guard is 0085DC96 FLDZ / FCOMI / 0085DCA0 JBE 0085DCAC, which sets the reciprocal to 0.0 via XORPS XMM0,XMM0 rather than dividing.
verification.data_audit: Full parse of all 259 .scn files in the shipped installation, not a sample. 133,655 localframe statements. The grep for the property-bag keys was run over the whole installation directory and hit only battlestationspacific.exe; the same grep finds CommandTarget in 257 of the 259 .scn files, so it is not failing on the format.
verification.body_coverage: 009258F0 complete (all 88 instructions). 00929C80 complete. 00928860 read to the call. 00924280 complete. 0085DC80 read as pseudocode in full plus the first 42 listing lines for the register ABI and the zero guard; its two arms' float arithmetic beyond the branch structure is not re-derived - partial. 0046CF40 read only at 0046D0E0..0046D222 and 0046D54B..0046D5E4 - partial, and it is not this packet's to own.

routines.abi: __thiscall(node /*ECX*/, hierarchyParent, worldNode, const float localFrame[16]) -> void, RET 0Ch

routines.name: BSP_Matrix_OrthonormalizeBasisRows
routines.abi: __fastcall(float m[16] /*ECX*/) -> void, plain RET, in place
routines.coverage: partial: the branch structure, the row roles, the zero guard and the two arms' shape are read; the individual float schedules inside each arm are not re-derived
routines.note: Gram-Schmidt over the three basis rows of a row-major 4x4. Row 2 (+20h) is the reference and is normalised first; |row1 . row2| is compared against the double 0.9990000128746033 at 00D0D0A0; below it row 1 is orthogonalised, normalised and row 0 = cross(row1, row2); above it row 0 takes that role and the cross product is negated through the float -0.0 at 00D7A208. The translation row is untouched. A zero row 2 survives as a zero row (the reciprocal is set to 0.0 rather than dividing) and then propagates into a zero row 0 through the cross product.

assumptions: That 00414DB0 composes world_child = local_child * world_parent without normalising, so a scaled root pose propagates down the subtree - carried over from docs/MATRIX_ORTHOGONAL_INVERSE.md, not re-derived here.
That 0042D0D0 runs with normalize = 0 and 00521370 takes asin of the raw y - same source. The pitch table in the audit is that formula with s filled in, not an independent derivation.
